42033-assyria.creator: A. H. Sayce, M.A.
42033-assyria.description: A book by A. H. Sayce, M.A.. Among the many wonderful achievements of the present century there is none more wonderful than the recovery and decipherment of the monuments of ancient Nineveh. For generations the great oppressing city had slept buried beneath the fragments of its own ruins, its history lost, its very site forgotten.

arxiv-2203-09944.title: Test Beam and Irradiation Facilities
arxiv-2203-09944.creator: M. Hartz, P. Merkel, E. Niner, E. Prebys, N. Toro
arxiv-2203-09944.description: Abstract Progress in particle physics depends on a multitude of unique facilities and capabilities that enable to advance detector technologies. Among others, key facilities involve test beams and irradiation facilities, which allow users to test the performance and lifetime of their detectors under realistic conditions.

arxiv-2302-09283.title: Convex subgraphs and spanning trees of the square cycles Thanks: *Corresponding author
arxiv-2302-09283.creator: Akihiro Munemasa, Yuuho Tanaka ∗
arxiv-2302-09283.description: Abstract . We classify connected spanning convex subgraphs of the square cycles. We then show that every spanning tree of C n 2 C_{n}^{2} is contained in a unique nontrivial connected spanning convex subgraph of C n 2 C_{n}^{2} .

arxiv-2310-02643.title: Online Algorithms for Spectral Hypergraph Sparsification
arxiv-2310-02643.creator: Tasuku Soma, Kam Chuen Tung, Yuichi Yoshida
arxiv-2310-02643.description: Abstract We provide the first online algorithm for spectral hypergraph sparsification. In the online setting, hyperedges with positive weights are arriving in a stream, and upon the arrival of each hyperedge, we must irrevocably decide whether or not to include it in the sparsifier.

arxiv-2407-18957.title: When AI Meets Finance (StockAgent): Large Language Model-based Stock Trading in Simulated Real-world Environments
arxiv-2407-18957.creator: Chong Zhang, Xinyi Liu, Zhongmou Zhang, Mingyu Jin, Lingyao Li, Zhenting Wang, Wenyue Hua, Dong Shu, Suiyuan Zhu, Xiaobo Jin, Sujian Li, Mengnan Du, Yongfeng Zhang
arxiv-2407-18957.description: Abstract . Can AI Agents simulate real-world trading environments to investigate the impact of external factors on stock trading activities (e.g., macroeconomics, policy changes, company fundamentals, and global events)? These factors, which frequently influence trading behaviors, are critical elements in the quest for maximizing investors’ profits. Our work attempts to solve this problem through large language model based agents.

arxiv-2410-08387.title: RUBIES: JWST/NIRSpec resolves evolutionary phases of dusty star-forming galaxies at z ∼ 2 z\sim 2 Facilities: ALMA, HST, JWST
arxiv-2410-08387.creator: Olivia R. Cooper, Gabriel Brammer, Kasper E. Heintz, Sune Toft, Caitlin M. Casey, David J. Setton, Anna de Graaff, Leindert Boogaard, Nikko J. Cleri, Steven Gillman, Rashmi Gottumukkala, Jenny E. Greene, Bitten Gullberg, Michaela Hirschmann, Raphael E. Hviding, Erini Lambrides, Joel Leja, Arianna S.
arxiv-2410-08387.description: Abstract The dearth of high quality spectroscopy of dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) — the main drivers of the assembly of dust and stellar mass at the peak of activity in the Universe — greatly hinders our ability to interpret their physical processes and evolutionary pathways.

arxiv-2410-10373.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Efficiently Selects Flatter Minima Late In Training
arxiv-2410-10373.creator: Zhanpeng Zhou, Mingze Wang, Yuchen Mao, Bingrui Li, Junchi Yan
arxiv-2410-10373.description: Abstract Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) has substantially improved the generalization of neural networks under various settings. Despite the success, its effectiveness remains poorly understood. In this work, we discover an intriguing phenomenon in the training dynamics of SAM, shedding light on understanding its implicit bias towards flatter minima over Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD).

arxiv-2506-12403.title: Bridging the Digital Divide: Small Language Models as a Pathway for Physics and Photonics Education in Underdeveloped Regions Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2506-12403.creator: Asghar Ghorbani, 1, *, Hanieh Fattahi, 2, 3, +
arxiv-2506-12403.description: Abstract Limited infrastructure, scarce educational resources, and unreliable internet access often hinder physics and photonics education in underdeveloped regions. These barriers create deep inequities in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education. This article explores how Small Language Models (SLMs)—compact, AI-powered tools that can run offline on low-power devices, offering a scalable solution.

arxiv-2511-13453.title: Hardware optimization on Android for inference of AI models
arxiv-2511-13453.creator: Iulius Gherasim, Carlos García Sánchez
arxiv-2511-13453.description: Abstract The pervasive integration of Artificial Intelligence models into contemporary mobile computing is notable across numerous use cases, from virtual assistants to advanced image processing. Optimizing the mobile user experience involves minimal latency and high responsiveness from deployed AI models with challenges from execution strategies that fully leverage real time constraints to the exploitation of heterogeneous hardware architecture.

pmc-10500404.title: Exploring the culture of faculty development: insights from Canadian leaders of faculty development
pmc-10500404.creator: Lerona Dana Lewis, Yvonne Steinert
pmc-10500404.description: BackgroundAlthough the word culture is frequently mentioned in research on faculty development (FD), the concept is rarely explored. This research aimed to examine the culture of FD in Canada, through the eyes of leaders of FD in the health professions.

pmc-10582936.title: COVID-19 booster prioritization in the West Bank: a survey experiment among Bedouins, refugees, and the majority group
pmc-10582936.creator: Sarah Carol, Ahmad Amro
pmc-10582936.description: IntroductionOur main aim is to understand to what extent Bedouins, internally displaced Palestinians (refugees) and majority-group members (non-refugees, non-Bedouins, settled) in the West Bank prioritize COVID-19 booster shots for their own group over other groups.MethodsWe conducted a survey experiment (face-to-face) among 678 Palestinians living in the West Bank.

pmc-12416662.title: Analysis of flavor formation and metabolite changes during production of Double-Layer Steamed Milk Custard made from buffalo milk
pmc-12416662.creator: Hong Lan, Xier Luo, Dingyun Xu, Kuiqing Cui, Ling Li, Chuan Li, Hao Qi, Qingyou Liu
pmc-12416662.description: Double-Layer Steamed Milk Custard (DLSMC) is a famous traditional Chinese dessert. This study aimed to analyze the flavor and the changes in metabolites during different stages of DLSMC preparation, including raw buffalo milk, thermo-processing, first and second-layer milk skin formation. Electronic nose and electronic tongue were employed to preliminarily assess the overall flavor characteristics between these stages.

pmc-12819519.title: Understanding machine learning weather prediction by designing a cost-efficient model with knowledge-oriented modules
pmc-12819519.creator: Minjong Cheon, Jeong-Hwan Kim, Yumi Choi, Yo-Hwan Choi, Seon-Yu Kang, Jeong-Gil Lee, Yoo-Geun Ham, Jin Young Kim, Daehyun Kang
pmc-12819519.description: Deep learning-based models are gaining prevalence in global weather forecasting, surpassing the performance of existing numerical models. However, training these models with high-resolution global weather data requires massive computational resources, making it difficult to conduct extensive experiments to understand the model processes.

pmc-13000350.title: Targeting the oxidative stress-neuroinflammation axis: the mechanism of arctigenin’s broad-spectrum analgesia with limited side effects
pmc-13000350.creator: Zhe Wang, Shu Li, Ping Lu, Jinglei Liao, Yimin Xu, Chen Lu, Weiwei Li, Jinhong Jiang
pmc-13000350.description: BackgroundArctigenin (AG), a natural lignan compound, has been reported to reveal its anti-inflammatory effects in glucose, lipid metabolism and type 2 diabetes mellitus. An increasing number of studies suggest that microglia activation evoked neuroinflammation is known to contribute to the development and progression of neuropathic pain.

pmc-13303798.title: Expanding the PHES-ODM: A Comprehensive, Open-Source Data Model for the Future of Wastewater-Based Epidemiology
pmc-13303798.creator: Mathew Thomson, Jean-David Therrien, Nikho Hizon, Janet Ting-mei Lin, Martin Wellman, Eugen-Sorin Sion, Carol Bennett, Peter A. Vanrolleghem, Douglas Manuel
pmc-13303798.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Wastewater surveillance (WWS) has quickly emerged as an invaluable tool for public health surveillance, particularly in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Its long-term utility is constrained, however, by fragmented data systems, inconsistent metadata practices, and poor interoperability. The Public Health and Environmental Surveillance Open Data Model (PHES-ODM) was developed as an open, collaborative framework to standardize WWS data and support transparent, ethical data use aligned with FAIR principles in response to these challenges.

pmc-13434731.title: Thioflavin-T derivatives with controlled AIE and ACQ properties as potential one-photon and two-photon amyloid markers
pmc-13434731.creator: Agata Hajda, Patryk Rybczyński, Weronika Andrzejczak, Borys Ośmiałowski, Joanna Olesiak-Bańska
pmc-13434731.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aggregates of organic dyes are not only interesting from a fundamental science perspective but also have significant implications in application as Aggregation Induced Emission (AIE) and Aggregation Caused Quenching (ACQ) dyes. Here, we present BF2-functionalized benzothiazoles, sharing the same core, but various electron-donating, amino groups substituted at the amino nitrogen by alkyl or aromatic groups and 1,4-phenylene acting as a conjugated bridge between donor and acceptor.
